Package sample.zenoh

Class ZenohJavaTlsPub

java.lang.Object
sample.zenoh.ZenohJavaTlsPub
public class ZenohJavaTlsPub extends Object
mTLS publisher sample: connects to a Zenoh router over TLS with client certificate authentication, publishes a fixed number of short UTF-8 payloads to a single key expression at a configurable interval, then closes the session cleanly. Sibling of ZenohJavaTlsSub; use ZenohJavaPub for plaintext TCP.

Positional CLI arguments (in order, only the first four are required):

  1. endpoint - Zenoh connect endpoint. Must start with tls/ (or wss/). No default; you must supply one, since a plaintext default here would defeat the point of this sample.
  2. rootCaCertPath - path to the CA root PEM used to verify the router's server certificate. Required.
  3. clientCertPath - path to the client leaf certificate PEM (mTLS). Required.
  4. clientKeyPath - path to the client private key PEM (mTLS). Required. PKCS#8 or SEC1 EC (unencrypted).
  5. keyExpr - publish key expression. Default demo/greeting.
  6. count - number of messages to publish. Default 5.
  7. interval - inter-message delay in milliseconds. Default 1000.

Optional named QoS / Timestamp / NodeId flags (accepted anywhere in args, in any order, stripped from the positional sequence before defaults apply): see ZenohJavaPub's class-level Javadoc for the full list. Same names, same semantics, same skip-when-default rules -- omitting them produces byte-identical wire output to the pre-QoS client.

  • --priority=<name>
  • --congestion=<drop|block>
  • --express
  • --auto-timestamp
  • --node-id=<u32>

Hostname verification is disabled in this sample. The typical field usage is connecting to an IP (e.g. a Tailscale / CGNAT 100.x.x.x address) where the router's server cert only lists hostnames as SANs -- the JDK's hostname verifier would reject on IP-to-CN mismatch. Trust is still anchored to the CA root; changing this is a one-line edit in main().

Pairs with ZenohJavaTlsSub for a quick end-to-end mTLS smoke test against a TLS-enabled zenohd.
